name: openslp
why: Service Location Protocol is a forgotten discovery protocol worth a look, though this implementation is deprecated.

brief.what_it_is: OpenSLP is an open-source implementation of the IETF Service Location Protocol (SLP), a standards-track protocol that lets networked applications discover where services are, and how they are configured, on enterprise networks. The homepage describes the project and its portability but does not describe the inputs or outputs in detail. The Homebrew formula installs an executable named slptool. Its description is 'Implementation of Service Location Protocol'.
brief.why_it_exists: The project aims to provide an open-source SLP implementation suitable for commercial and non-commercial use. The homepage argues that no other service advertising or location system has offered a feature set as complete and important for mission-critical enterprise applications as SLP.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps beyond pointing to SourceForge for source code and binaries. It lists platforms it has been ported to: Linux (32/64), Windows (32/64), SCO Unix, FreeBSD, Solaris, Tru64, Mac OS X, Darwin, and Irix. I did not find a runtime, account, or configuration requirement on the homepage.
brief.standout: SLP is a discovery protocol that most people have never used, and the homepage frames it as a mature, standards-track option for enterprise service location. It is an old, widely ported implementation of a protocol that has had annual RFC enhancements and new service templates.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage footer reads 'Copyright © 2011 openslp.org', and the page has no release notes, last-commit date, or version number. The scout notes describe the implementation as deprecated, but I could not confirm that from the homepage. Only the homepage was fetched; the SourceForge and download pages were not reachable through links in the fetched text.
brief.caveats: The homepage is dated (copyright 2011) and points to SourceForge for the actual code, so the page may not reflect current development. The scout notes call this implementation deprecated, which I could not verify from the page. The license is the Caldera Systems open source license, which the homepage calls legally compatible with BSD. The homepage lists no commands, usage examples, or install instructions, so the slptool command's behavior is unverified here.
quotes: Service Location Protocol (SLP) is an Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) standards track protocol that provides a framework to allow networking applications to discover the existence, location, and configuration of networked services in enterprise networks.
The OpenSLP project is an effort to develop an open-source implementation of the IETF Service Location Protocol suitable for commercial and non-commercial application.

While other service advertising and location methods have been invented and even widely consumed, no other system thus far has provided a feature set as complete and as important to mission-critical enterprise applications as SLP.
fetch_log: http://www.openslp.org — fetched OK; HTML homepage with About, Download, Contribute, Documentation, and Credits sections. The download and documentation pages were not followed because their URLs were not present in the fetched text.
